hints: A pile gives you items in reverse order. What happens to the order if you pour one pile into a second pile?
Use two stacks: in receives every push; out serves pop and peek. Only when out is empty, move everything from in to out — that reverses the order so the oldest item ends up on top.

1. push(x): push onto in.
  2. Helper shift(): if out is empty, pop everything from in and push it onto out.
  3. pop(): shift, then pop from out.
  4. peek(): shift, then peek at out.
  5. empty(): both stacks are empty.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: On every push, move all items to a helper stack, push x, and move them back so the front stays on top.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: In/out stacks; refill out only when it is empty, so each item moves at most once.

explain: In the sample, push 4 and push 9 go onto in = [4, 9] (9 on top). peek finds out empty, so it pours: out becomes [9, 4] with 4 on top, and returns 4. pop removes that 4. empty is false because 9 is still in out. The rule 'only refill when out is empty' is essential: items already in out are older than anything in in, so mixing them would break FIFO order. Each item is moved once, giving amortised O(1).
recognize: Build a FIFO structure from LIFO stacks → two stacks, pour one into the other lazily.
